verified.name: Engine Ventures
verified.thesis: Engine Ventures invests in early-stage Tough Tech companies developing hardware-based technologies across deep tech fields including biotech, robotics, green energy, agriculture, manufacturing, material science, and quantum computing.
verified.notes: Engine Ventures is a separate investment firm that spun out from The Engine (a nonprofit incubator/accelerator founded by MIT in 2016) in 2023. The Engine is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit as of 2025. Key distinction: Engine Ventures is the VC fund; The Engine is the nonprofit accelerator/incubator. Wikipedia article is titled 'The Engine (organization)' but covers both entities. No current senior partners explicitly named on firm website or Wikipedia for Engine Ventures specifically. AUM not verified in sources.

changesProposed.name: General Catalyst

verified.name: General Catalyst
verified.thesis: General Catalyst invests across seed, venture, and growth stages. The firm focuses on transforming critical institutions with applied AI, particularly in healthcare and defense.
verified.notes: In June 2024, General Catalyst acquired La Famiglia (German VC firm) and Venture Highway (New Delhi-based early-stage investor). In October 2024, firm raised $8B in new funds. In December 2025, agreed to acquire Janus Henderson for ~$7.4B (later increased offer to $52/share in March 2026). In May 2025, launched £30M NHS MedTech venture fund. Jeannette zu Fürstenberg became managing director overseeing European business following La Famiglia acquisition.

changesProposed.name: Y Combinator

verified.name: Y Combinator
verified.thesis: Y Combinator invests $500,000 per company ($125,000 for 7% equity on post-money SAFE and $375,000 on uncapped SAFE with MFN clause) in a select group of startups accepted into four annual batches. The three-month intensive program provides office hours, mentorship, and community support to help startups achieve product-market fit and better shape for fundraising.
verified.notes: Garry Tan became President & CEO in January 2023. Jared Friedman succeeded Michael Seibel as Managing Partner in March 2024. Headquarters relocated from Mountain View to San Francisco in spring 2023. Tom Blomfield and Brad Flora listed in database entry but not found in current source materials.
